title: Relative q-power Frobenius of Y_0 ×_{k_0} k
statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum $(p,a,q,k_0,k)$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber]. Let $Y_0$ be a $k_0$-scheme [def-weil-scheme-over-base] of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] and let $Y=Y_0\times_{k_0}k$ be its geometric fiber. Since $p=0$ in $k_0$, $Y_0$ is of characteristic $p$; its absolute $q$-power Frobenius $\operatorname{Fr}^{(q)}_{Y_0}:Y_0\to Y_0$ [def-weil-absolute-frobenius-scheme] is a morphism of $k_0$-schemes, because the absolute Frobenius commutes with the structure morphism $Y_0\to\operatorname{Spec}k_0$ (Stacks, Lemma 33.36.2, tag 0CC8) and $\operatorname{Fr}^{(q)}_{\operatorname{Spec}k_0}=\operatorname{id}$ as $c^q=c$ for $c\in k_0$. The *relative ($q$-power) Frobenius* of $Y$ over $k$ is its base change [def-pc-base-change] to $k$,

$$
 F_Y=\operatorname{Fr}^{(q)}_{Y_0}\times_{k_0}\operatorname{id}_k:Y\longrightarrow Y,
$$

a morphism of $k$-schemes; on an affine open $\operatorname{Spec}A_0\subseteq Y_0$ it is $\operatorname{Spec}$ of the $k$-algebra endomorphism $a\otimes b\mapsto a^q\otimes b$ of $A_0\otimes_{k_0}k$.

source.place: (1.1.14), p. 153 (pdf p. 18): 'F : X → X est l'endomorphisme de Frobenius de X, déduit par extension des scalaires de l'endomorphisme de Frobenius x ↦ x^q de X_0 (lequel est F_q-linéaire)'; cf. Stacks, Varieties, Definition 33.36.4 (tag 0CC9), of which F_Y is the $q$-power version composed with $Y^{(q/k)}\cong Y$
